meta.vehicle: Mahindra Thar Roxx · Thar Digital Services

entries.notes: Pushed past Agra — Agra-Lucknow Expressway was too good to stop on. Roxx on cruise with ADAS, just zoomed. Reached Gomti Nagar by 9:30 PM. Ate dinner, slept well.

hotel.name: The Grand JBR
hotel.location: CF-129 Viraj Khand, Gomti Nagar, Lucknow

entries.delta: ↑ Pushed 389 km past planned Agra halt — Agra-Lucknow Expressway is cruise-control fast

events.text: Agra-Lucknow Expressway · ADAS + cruise did most of the work. Quality so high we ate the planned Agra halt and pushed 389 km past plan in one shot.

entries.route: Purvanchal · Gorakhpur Link · NH27 · Sunauli border
entries.notes: Left Lucknow 8 AM after breakfast. Purvanchal + Gorakhpur Link expressways smooth — easy morning run. Last ~95 km on NH27 was regular road. Got to Sunauli by 2 PM but then 1.5 hours crawling through trucks before the border, then 44 minutes doing the Bhansar paperwork. Crossed into Nepal, continued ~25 km to Butwal.

events.text: Nepal TIV online portal (nnsw.gov.np/tiv/gen) — failed at last step, no QR generated. Indian domestic cards / UPI not supported. Did physical Bhansar instead — 44 minutes.
~1.5 h truck-traffic crawl approaching Sunauli border. Plan earlier next time.

entries.notes:
Breakfast at the Dreamland café in Butwal. Rolled out at 9:30 AM. Siddhartha Highway up to Pokhara — winding mountain road, the Roxx ate the corners.

### Road stops · Butwal → Pokhara
- **Coffee break** — pulled over for a cup to keep the wheel hand awake on the climb.
- **Momo halt** — roadside dhaba stop, hot momos, solid trail fuel.
- **Footbridge over a valley** — couldn't drive past it. A suspension footbridge strung across a deep valley, swaying in the breeze. Parked the Thar, walked across, clicked pictures, walked back.

Reached Pokhara in the afternoon, checked into the **[Waterfront Resort](https://maps.app.goo.gl/?q=28.2217546,83.9516047)**.

### Evening · first Lakeside walk
- Strolled along Lakeside, dropped in at **[The Juicery Cafe](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=The+Juicery+Cafe+Pokhara+Lakeside)** right on the water — late, proper, no-rush lunch with the lake right there.
- Wandered up to the **[Pokhara Disneyland](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Pokhara+Disneyland+Lakeside+Khara+Pokhara)** side, sat on the grass by the lake, just sat. No agenda.
- That hour or two by the water was the trip's first proper *we made it* moment. Wind, water, no honking, no driving brief. The whole stretch is quietly serene in a way you don't really plan for.
entries.delta: ↑ Arrived Pokhara 1 day ahead of original plan (was Day 4 / 12 May)

events.text: Footbridge stop on the Siddhartha Highway · suspension bridge over a deep valley, worth pulling over for. Note location next time — no signage, easy to miss.
The Juicery Cafe (North Lakeside) — first sit-down meal in Pokhara. Lake view, healthy plates, juices. Easy choice for a long arrival lunch.
Pokhara Disneyland lakeshore · the grassy strip just north of Tal Barahi. Sit-on-the-grass kind of place, lake right there, evening light is everything.

entries.notes:
Slept in — up by 9. Breakfast at the Waterfront, took my morning stand-up from the room.

- Walked into Lakeside aiming for [White Rabbit](https://maps.app.goo.gl/?q=28.2096886,83.9568973) or [Cafe Camellia](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Cafe+Camellia+Street+16+Lakeside+Pokhara), but stopped earlier at **[The Grounds By Majestic Lakefront](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=The+Grounds+By+Majestic+Lakefront+Pokhara)** — coffee, took office calls till 2.
- Walked east through the Pokhara bazaar; finally settled at **[White Rabbit](https://maps.app.goo.gl/?q=28.2096886,83.9568973)** and worked till 4:45 PM.
- Closed laptops and wandered the market — picked up fridge magnets and small souvenirs.
- Tried to catch **[Movie Garden](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Movie+Garden+Pokhara)** — Google Maps wouldn't point at the right approach; finally found it via Street 21 near Tipsy Town Restaurant *(note for future)*. Queued 30 min — tickets sold out at the counter.
- Walked back to Lakeside, dinner at **[Open House Restro and Lounge Bar](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Open+House+Restro+And+Lounge+Bar+Pokhara)** by the lake.
- Back to the hotel ~10 PM.
entries.delta: Rest day — no driving. Worked remote from two Lakeside cafés.

events.text: Worked from The Grounds By Majestic Lakefront (morning) and White Rabbit Coffee (afternoon). Both have fast wifi + outlets, lakeside-walkable from Waterfront.
Movie Garden — Google Maps doesn't pin the approach correctly. Walk in via Street 21 (near Tipsy Town Restaurant). Tickets sell out fast — got to the counter after 30 min queue and they were gone.
Pokhara bazaar (east of Lakeside) — picked up fridge magnets + small souvenirs. Walkable from White Rabbit.

entries.leg: Pokhara · Sarangkot sunrise + Mustang prep + lake-north drive
entries.notes:
Long day split into two halves — pre-dawn Sarangkot sortie, then back to base for work and a full afternoon of Mustang-prep errands that drifted into a lake-north drive.

### Pre-dawn · Sarangkot sunrise run
- Up at 3 AM. Left the Waterfront by 4 AM — early-start strategy to dodge the daybreak tourist-taxi convoy and grab parking right below the **[Sarangkot View Tower](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Sarangkot+View+Tower+Pokhara)** entrance.
- Plan worked: reached the entrance gate by 4:40 AM. Just one other car there, ample parking.
- Walked up, bought tickets, climbed the tower deck. Sunrise was billed for 5:20 AM.
- Cloud cover held the sun behind a wall — no clean reveal at 5:20. Stayed gauzy; didn't punch through till much later. The mountain panorama itself was still up there, just softer than the brochure version.

### Afternoon · Mustang prep + lake-north drive
- Back at the Waterfront — breakfast then work from the room till afternoon. Took the Thar out for the Mustang-prep errands.
- **Permits at [Nepal Tourism Board · Damside](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Nepal+Tourism+Board+Damside+Pokhara+ACAP+office)** — picked up the **ACAP** (Annapurna Conservation Area Permit) for both of us. Muktinath sits inside the Annapurna conservation zone, so this is the one you need; no Restricted Area Permit since we're staying in Lower Mustang. 1000 NPR/SAARC head, 2K total, in-and-out in 20 minutes.
- Lunch + work at **[Fresh Elements Restaurant & Bar](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Fresh+Elements+Restaurant+Pokhara)** (Middle Path · Street 16). Carried laptops, ate slow, kept working after the plates went away.
- Parked on Lakeside Road, walked the market and **exchanged INR → NPR** — stocking cash for Mustang where the internet thins out past Beni and most counters take cash, usually NPR.
- Drizzle escalated to a proper pour late afternoon; rushed back to the Thar.
- Drove home past the hotel and **kept going north toward [Pame](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Pame+Pokhara)**. Pulled over on the green patch by the lake right in front of **[The Beach Bar and Lodge](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=The+Beach+Bar+and+Lodge+Pokhara+Khapaudi)** (Khapaudi) — a waitress politely asked to move the car, it was blocking the lake view from the resort tables. While I was repositioning, a guest came out specifically to photograph the Thar Roxx — Ukrainian, big jeep fan, knew Mahindra made an "Indian Wrangler" but had never seen one in the wild. Good chat. Photo of the car now lives in a stranger's phone in Kyiv, which is a quietly weird thing to think about.
- Pushed further north till the entrance of a small village (name starting with **B** — escaped us in the moment, *note to grab off offline maps later*). Turned around as it got dark.
- **Skipped [Pumdikot Shiva Statue](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Pumdikot+Shiva+Statue+Pokhara)** — could see the hilltop from the lake-north stop, completely socked in by cloud. No view today.
- Back to the Waterfront, dinner, slept.
entries.delta: Pre-dawn Sarangkot run + half-day office work + Mustang prep + an unplanned lake-north loop.

events.text: Sarangkot sunrise · clouded over. Scheduled 5:20 AM, sun didn't break through cleanly. Mountain silhouette visible, but no postcard reveal.
Sarangkot parking · leaving Lakeside by 4 AM beats the tourist-taxi rush. By 5 AM the lot fills, by 5:15 AM cars park down-slope. Pre-dawn run = front-row spot at the gate.
ACAP permit · Nepal Tourism Board, Damside (NTNC Building, Pardi). 1000 NPR per SAARC head — Indian nationals qualify. 20 min counter time. Muktinath = Lower Mustang = ACAP only, no RAP needed.
INR→NPR cash swap done. Stock enough — internet gets patchy past Beni, most counters in Mustang are cash-first and NPR-only.

Thar Roxx photo-op at Khapaudi · Ukrainian guest at The Beach Bar came out to shoot the car. Knew Mahindra made an 'Indian Wrangler,' first time seeing one in real life. (Bonus: also asked to move the car — was blocking the lake view from the resort tables.)
Skipped Pumdikot Shiva Statue — hilltop completely cloud-wrapped from the lake-side view. Try on a clearer day.

entries.leg: Pokhara · rest day + chores + last-night spin
entries.notes:
Decided to absorb today as an extra rest day in Pokhara instead of heading for Beni — sleep debt from yesterday's 3 AM start, Mustang chores still pending. Plan: leave for Muktinath at first light on **2026-05-15**.

### Morning · slow + office
- Up around 9. Lazy breakfast at the Waterfront. Office work from the room till lunchtime.

### Afternoon · cave temple + the underground waterfall
- Drove south to **[Gupteshwar Mahadev Cave Temple](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Gupteshwor+Mahadev+Cave+Pokhara+Chhorepatan)** (Pokhara-17, Chhorepatan, near the airport). A long spiral staircase drops you into the cave — Shiva shrine at the top, a *lying Vishnu* statue at a lower level, and at the deepest point a window onto the **waterfall inside the cave itself**. The same water you see crashing into Devi's Fall above goes underground here. Genuinely serene — not like any cave-temple I've seen in India.
- Crossed the road to **[Devi's Fall · Patale Chhango](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Devi%27s+Fall+Patale+Chhango+Pokhara)** — same water, viewed from the top. *Half the site was closed off for construction*, so the full circuit wasn't open. Pictures from what was open, then moved on.

### Late lunch · Cafe Camellia
- Back to Lakeside for lunch at **[Cafe Camellia](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Cafe+Camellia+Street+16+Lakeside+Pokhara)** (Street 16). *Parking was rough — note for next time, plan to walk in.* The cafe itself is gorgeous — well-designed interior, garden vibe, **two resident dogs** that came to say hi while we ate (~4 PM). Slow lunch, took a short office call from the table.

### Evening · Pumdikot Shiva, despite the clouds
- ~6 PM the drizzle started picking up. We went anyway — even knowing the Annapurna view was off the table, the **drive itself** was worth it. Tight twisties up to **[Pumdikot Shiva Statue](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Pumdikot+Shiva+Statue+Pokhara)** — almost 45° gradients, hairpin U-turns, exactly the kind of road the Roxx is built for.
- Made it to the statue by 6:45 (it closes at 7). Quick walk around the platform, a few pictures, and out.
- **The descent stole the day**: post-sunset, the whole Pokhara basin was lit up — lake, highway, Lakeside cafes, all glittering. Stopped at a cliff pullout for ~10 minutes to just watch it.

### Mustang prep · supplies + fuel + cash
- Lakeside mart for **snacks and supplies** for the Muktinath run.
- Filled the Roxx to the brim — *next reliable diesel is Beni, and that's the last pump before Mustang.* Crucial.
- Topped up the **INR → NPR cash** buffer one more time, just to be safe past Beni.

### Dinner
- Walked over to **[The Grounds By Majestic Lakefront](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=The+Grounds+By+Majestic+Lakefront+Pokhara)** for dinner — closed for the night. Left the Thar in their lot and walked to **[Annapurna Garden Cafe & Lounge](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Annapurna+Garden+Cafe+Lounge+Pokhara+Lakeside)** — simple, no-fuss dinner.
- Back to the Waterfront, organising + packing for tomorrow. Sleep.
entries.delta: Held one day longer in Pokhara to bank sleep + finish Mustang prep — depart for Muktinath at first light tomorrow.

events.text: Gupteshwar Mahadev Cave Temple (Chhorepatan, opposite Devi's Fall) · spiral staircase down to a Shiva shrine + lying-Vishnu murti + the same waterfall that disappears at Devi's Fall above. Quietest cave-temple either of us has been in.
Devi's Fall · Patale Chhango — partially closed for construction. Go for the cave-side view (Gupteshwar) if the falls side is fenced off.
Cafe Camellia (Street 16 Lakeside) · gorgeous interior, two resident dogs, great late-lunch spot. *Parking is rough — try walking in from a side street.*
Pumdikot Shiva Statue · closes 7 PM sharp. Even on a clouded-out day the *drive itself* is worth it — steep twisty road, hairpin U-turns. The night-descent view of lit-up Pokhara is the real reward.
Mustang fuel · tanked the Roxx to the brim at Lakeside. The last reliable diesel before Muktinath is at **Beni** — fuel up there too. No bowsers in Mustang you'd want to rely on.
Mustang supplies · snacks + bottled water + INR-to-NPR top-up done at Lakeside before departure. Internet thins past Beni, cash is king from there.
Dinner plan went sideways · The Grounds By Majestic was closed at our hour. Walked over to Annapurna Garden Cafe & Lounge for a simple dinner — open till 2 AM, easy fallback.

entries.route: Baglung Hwy · Beni-Jomsom Rd · Kali Gandaki valley
entries.notes:
The day every AI tool, every blog, every itinerary builder — including my own — said would need *three days minimum* (Pokhara → Tatopani → Jomsom → Muktinath, with overnight halts to acclimatise). We did it in **half a day**, then walked into the temple the same afternoon.

### Pokhara → Muktinath, in one push
- Out of the **Waterfront** at **6:30 AM**, fearing the unknown.
- Quick chai at a roadside stall on the Baglung Highway — first snow-capped peaks of the trip in the windscreen view.
- Road quality fell off in stages, almost like a difficulty ladder:
  - **3-lane highway** out of Pokhara →
  - **2-lane highway** Pokhara → Beni →
  - **Single lane** after Beni →
  - **Gravel + broken tarmac** past Tatopani →
  - **Actual river bed** in places, where you just drive the dry rocks →
  - One stretch where **three workers were live-drilling a hillside with a jackhammer** to widen the cut enough for two vehicles to pass each other. Watched them work, then squeezed through.
- Afternoon **rain showers without clouds** — sun and water at the same time, falling through the Kali Gandaki valley. Massive river below, scenery the brochures don't earn.
- Jomsom at **12:30 PM**. Stopped at **[Xanadu Homes](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Xanadu+Homes+Jomsom+Mustang)** (near Jomsom airport — the Lavazza branding on the board is what caught the eye) for coffee + a *home-made apple pie*. Looked at each other and went "…we have the whole day. Should we just push?"
- **Muktinath at 1:45 PM**. ~7 h door-to-door.

### Parking + room scramble
- Private cars aren't allowed inside the temple campus before 6 PM. Parked at **[Lo Mustang Himalayan Resort](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Lo+Mustang+Himalayan+Resort+Ranipauwa+Muktinath)** (Ranipauwa) to ask about a room.
- Their 2-pax rooms were sold out, but the manager *made calls on our behalf* and got us a deluxe room at **[Hotel de Purang](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Hotel+de+Purang+Ranipauwa+Muktinath)** — tea on the house at Lo Mustang while we waited for the confirmation. Genuinely above-and-beyond service.
- Walked over to Purang (car stays at Lo Mustang till 6 PM gate-open). Checked in by 3:30 PM.

### Temple — done the same day
- Got told the temple was open till **7 PM** — meaning we could do darshan today and use tomorrow for the return drive. Net: **trip compressed by one full day vs every planning source we read.**
- The walk to the temple from Ranipauwa is the part nobody talks about: **~300 stairs at 3,810 m**. The altitude makes ordinary stairs into an actual workout. *Worth flagging for anyone reading this who's preparing — the hike-in is not a footnote.*
- **Mukti Dhara · the 108 sacred water spouts** in a semicircle behind the main shrine — stone bull-face spouts. Took the running ice-water bath under all 108 (the *moksha* tradition). Did the darshan inside.
- **Jwala Mai gompa** — the eternal flame fed by natural gas seeping through the rock, beside a small spring. Quiet, dim, unforgettable.
- **Buddha statue + the surrounding gompas** — clicked around the campus, kept walking.

### Roxx earns its flags
- Street shopping on the way back — picked up gifts for home, and a string of **Himalayan prayer flags for the Roxx**. The car has now been on legitimately treacherous-to-non-existent roads and topped out at **~12,500 ft / 3,810 m** — it has earned the flags.

### The cafe encounter that shouldn't have happened
- Late lunch at **[Hotel Bob Marley](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Hotel+Bob+Marley+Muktinath)** cafe. While ordering, recognised a familiar face — [**Mr Siva**](https://www.instagram.com/sivafromsun/), who I'd only seen in **[Sriman Kotaru](https://www.youtube.com/@SrimanKotaru)**'s videos. Sriman lives near my home in **Kondapur, Hyderabad** — and so does Siva. We've never met in Hyderabad. We met *here.*
- Siva rode in on his **BMW R1250 GS** from Hyderabad. With him: **Amit**, on a **Triumph Tiger** from Pune. They met in Jabalpur, rode to Gorakhpur, did **Upper Mustang for the Tibet festival**, and were rolling back down through Muktinath.
- Two solo bikes, two cities, one cafe at 3,800 m. The probabilities don't math.

### Wrap
- Back to **Hotel de Purang** to rest, freshen up, hot shower.
- 6:50 PM — got the Thar inside the village (campus gate now open). Tucked into the hotel lot.
- Dinner: a proper Nepali **daal bhaat**. Slept.
entries.delta: ↑↑ Pokhara → Muktinath in half a day. Every AI / blog / itinerary said this needs 3+ days. Darshan done the same afternoon — entire Mustang loop now compressed by 1+ days.

events.text: Pokhara → Muktinath in ~7 hours flat · 6:30 AM start, Jomsom 12:30 PM, Muktinath 1:45 PM. Every planning source (Gemini, blogs, my own pre-trip itinerary) called for 3 days minimum with overnight halts at Tatopani + Jomsom. Reality: one push works if you start early and the road gods are kind.

Road conditions step down in stages past Pokhara · 3-lane → 2-lane → single → gravel → literal river bed. One stretch had three workers actively jackhammering a hillside to make passing-room for two cars. Beyond Beni you are in 4WD territory — the Roxx was the right vehicle for this.

Coffee + home-made apple pie pit stop at Xanadu Homes (Jomsom, near the airport). Lavazza branding on the board got our attention from the road — turned out to be the perfect 'do we keep going?' decision point.
Muktinath temple campus closed to private cars before 6 PM. Park at Ranipauwa village (Lo Mustang Himalayan Resort lot works) and walk in. Gate opens for vehicles after 6 PM.

Lo Mustang Himalayan Resort manager · rooms sold out but made calls and arranged a deluxe at Hotel de Purang for us, comp'd a tea while we waited. The kind of hospitality that justifies recommending a hotel even when you don't end up staying there.

The 300 stairs to the temple at 3,810 m are the unsung effort of this trip · planning sources fixate on the drive and skip the climb. At altitude, ordinary stairs become a workout — pace yourself, drink water, don't sprint.

Mukti Dhara · the 108 sacred water spouts (stone bull-face dharas in a semicircle behind the main shrine) + the running ice-water bath = the moksha tradition. Did it. The water is glacier-cold, the path is short, the experience is worth it.
Jwala Mai gompa · the eternal flame fed by natural gas seeping through the rock, burning beside a small spring. Quiet shrine, easy to miss in the rush to the main temple — don't.
Himalayan prayer flags · tied to the Roxx at 12,500 ft (3,810 m). The car has now done legitimately broken roads to a treacherous altitude and earned the flag-string. Symbolic, sure. Felt right.

Met Mr Siva (@sivafromsun) at Hotel Bob Marley · friend of Hyderabadi YouTuber Sriman Kotaru, lives in Kondapur — same neighbourhood as my home. Rode solo from Hyderabad to Upper Mustang on his BMW R1250 GS, met Amit (Triumph Tiger, Pune) en route in Jabalpur. They went to Upper Mustang for the Tibet festival and were stopping at Muktinath on the way back. Two cities, one cafe at 3,800 m — pure improbability.

entries.route: Kali Gandaki valley descent · Beni-Jomsom Rd · Baglung Hwy
entries.notes:
Plan was a 5:20 AM wake-up for sunrise. Reality: woke up to a headache, looked out the window — cloud-wall, no sunrise. Phone said it had been **-2 °C overnight**. Tried to sleep, headache kept building. By 6:45 AM we'd named it: **possible AMS, time to lose altitude.**

### Descent · Muktinath → Pokhara
- Packed, breakfast at Purang, on the road by **8 AM**.
- **Jomsom by 9 AM**. Second stop at **[Xanadu Homes](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Xanadu+Homes+Jomsom+Mustang)** — 40 minute break, hot coffee, headache started lifting noticeably with the altitude loss.
- Just past Jomsom airport, a no-road patch with **two European backpackers thumbing a lift** — full trekking kit, French accents. Dinki said *we should help.* I stopped.

### Hitchhikers · Valentina + Gabe → Tatopani
- **Valentina** — architecture student from France. **Gabe** — also French, builds websites, previously lived out of a **Toyota Prado with a roof-tent in Australia**, camping wherever the day ended. Wild backstory.
- Heading to Tatopani. Loaded their packs into the boot.
- The drive disappeared into conversation: cars, **French vs Indian weddings**, **Hinduism's overlap with Jainism**, Valentina's Golden Triangle trip (Agra-Delhi-Jaipur) and her notes on Indian cities, Gabe's road-trip philosophy. They liked the Roxx — Valentina actually said *"you have a nice car."*
- Dropped them at Tatopani. Swapped a company card. Two strangers, a sliver of two countries, gone. The rough road that gutted us on the way up didn't even register on the way down.

### Tatopani → Pokhara
- Lunch-break at **Beni** — proper plate of chowmein, the kind that hits exactly right after a mountain morning.
- Hit **Pokhara just as the rain went heavy**. Decided not to drive into Lakeside in a downpour — checked into **[Lake View Resort](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Lake+View+Resort+Pokhara+Lakeside)** (Lakeside, the one with Fishtail visible from the property).

### The Siva coincidence, part 2
- Pulled into the resort's parking and clocked a **BMW R1250 GS with a Telangana plate** sitting there. Instantly recognised it — that's **Siva's bike**, the same Siva we'd met at Hotel Bob Marley in Muktinath yesterday. Two cities, two hotels, *one parking lot*. The probabilities just won't stop.
- Rain eased. We ran into Siva and Amit on their way out for lunch — quick hi, then we crashed in the rooms because the AMS headache was still there. Real sleep, finally.

### Evening · slow recovery
- Up around 7:30 PM, freshened up.
- **Light rain still on** — bought umbrellas on the way out.
- Dinner at **[Cafe Camellia](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Cafe+Camellia+Street+16+Lakeside+Pokhara)** (Street 16) — calm, gorgeous interior we already love.
- Slow walk down Lakeside in the drizzle.
- Picked up **ground coffee** for home from **[Himalayan Java Coffee · Lakeside](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Himalayan+Java+Coffee+Lakeside+Pokhara)** — proper Nepali arabica, easy travel-home gift.
- Back to the hotel, sleep.
entries.delta: ↓ Descended to recover from suspected AMS. Headache lifted with altitude loss — sea-level math is real.

events.text: AMS at Muktinath · woke up with a building headache after overnight temp hit -2°C at 3,810 m. Lesson: when in doubt at altitude, descend. Headache started lifting noticeably by Jomsom (2,720 m), gone by Pokhara (827 m).

Hitchhikers picked up just past Jomsom airport · Valentina (French architecture student) + Gabe (French, ex-Australia overlander in a roof-tent Prado). Trekkers heading to Tatopani. The 4-hour drive evaporated in the conversation — cars, weddings, Hinduism/Jainism, Australian campervan life. Probably the best random encounter of the trip so far.

The Siva coincidence, part 2 · pulled into Lake View Resort's parking in Pokhara and saw the same BMW R1250 GS with the Telangana plate we'd parked next to at Hotel Bob Marley in Muktinath yesterday. Different city, different hotel, same parking lot. At some point a coincidence becomes a pattern.
Beni chowmein break · roadside plate, exactly the right thing after a mountain descent.
Himalayan Java Lakeside · picked up ground coffee for home. 100% Nepali arabica, easy travel-back gift. They have multiple Pokhara branches — Lakeside is the one with the upstairs view over Phewa.

entries.route: Prithvi Highway · via Bandipur · Mugling · Thamel
entries.notes:
Lazy start to a long drive. Clear weather meant the snow-capped peaks were actually visible from Lakeside streets this morning — a goodbye view Pokhara hadn't shown us before.

### Morning · slow Pokhara goodbye
- Slept in. Breakfast at the resort.
- Walked the lake, clicked a few last pictures — clearest sky of the whole stay, snow-cap silhouettes from the street itself.
- Back to the hotel, packed for Kathmandu.
- **At checkout**: saw **Siva and Amit** in the parking lot trying to repair a puncture on Amit's Triumph Tiger — *their inflator battery was dead.* Pulled the Thar's inflator out of the trunk and handed it over. Job done, swapped a company card, said goodbye. **Third encounter with the Siva-Amit duo across three locations.** Pattern fully confirmed.

### Prithvi Highway · Pokhara → Kathmandu
- **204 km, ~6.5 h door-to-door.** First 90 km is genuinely smooth highway — covered it in **~1 h 20 m**. Average pace gives a false read of the rest of the day.
- After ~90 km Google Maps was still showing 4 h to Kathmandu with only 110 km left. That ratio tells you everything: **the back half of Prithvi Highway is a fight.** Comparable to the Muktinath approach road, no joke. Single carriageway, traffic, broken sections, slow-trucks.
- Stopped at **[Himalayan Java](https://maps.app.goo.gl/Rd2zrYeoHDQRGDyt6)** near **Bandipur** — coincidentally located *above a Mahindra showroom.* Felt symmetrical, given the car. Solid break.
- **Kathmandu border hit by 4:30 PM.** The sensory step-change is dramatic — Pokhara's calm to Kathmandu's chaos in one ring-road crossing. Urbanisation, traffic, crowd density, noise. Took a beat to adjust.

### Thamel · first impressions
- Checked into **[Hotel Thrive · A Tropical Courtyard](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Hotel+Thrive+Tropical+Courtyard+Thamel+Kathmandu)** — Thamel, secure parking (the deciding factor), walkable to everything we wanted to see.
- In by 6 PM, freshened up, back on the street by 7. Starving by then.
- **Dinner at [Roadhouse Cafe · Thamel](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Roadhouse+Cafe+Thamel+Kathmandu)** — heard the wood-fired pizza reputation, went for it.
- Walked Thamel afterwards. Different beast from anywhere we've been on this trip — heavily commercialised, busy, chaotic, no proper footpaths, shops piled on shops. Honestly **reminded me of the old quarters of Jaipur / Jodhpur** — same narrow-lane character, same density.
- After the serenity of Pokhara and the Mustang week, Thamel felt like sensory overload. Got bored faster than expected.
- Back to the hotel, slept. Tired from the drive.
entries.delta: → Spontaneous Kathmandu addition. Mustang ran 1.5 days ahead of plan; reinvesting that surplus into KTM + Chitwan instead of more Pokhara work days.

events.text: The Siva coincidence, part 3 · ran into Siva + Amit again in the Lake View Resort parking lot at checkout — they were fighting a puncture on Amit's Tiger with a dead inflator. Loaned them the Roxx's spare inflator, problem solved. Three encounters across three locations now — Muktinath cafe → Pokhara hotel parking → Pokhara hotel checkout.

Prithvi Highway is two roads in one · the first 90 km out of Pokhara is smooth fast highway (we did it in 1h20). The last ~110 km into Kathmandu is closer to the Muktinath approach — single lane, broken patches, slow truck convoys. Plan ~6.5 h door-to-door, not the 4 h Google promises.
Himalayan Java pit-stop near Bandipur · sits above a Mahindra showroom on the Prithvi Highway. Useful break point about halfway between Pokhara and Kathmandu, especially if you're driving a Mahindra.

Pokhara → Kathmandu sensory step-change · the ring-road crossing flips you from mountain-lake calm to dense urban chaos in one transition. Mentally prep for it — first impressions of Thamel hit harder if you've come straight from Lakeside.
Roadhouse Cafe Thamel · wood-fired pizza, original Thamel branch. Solid early-dinner choice — walking distance from Hotel Thrive.

Thamel · heavily commercialised, narrow lanes, no real footpaths, shops stacked on shops. Felt very similar to old Jaipur / Jodhpur city cores. Bring patience and don't expect Pokhara-style breathing room.

entries.leg: Kathmandu · Kopan + Boudha + Pashupatinath + Thamel night
entries.route: Thamel · Kopan · Boudhanath · Pashupatinath · Sinamangal · Thamel
entries.notes:
Monday — office work in the morning, full Kathmandu day-out from lunch onwards.

### Morning · work + sleep debt
- Slept in (Pokhara → Kathmandu drive carried over). Late breakfast at Hotel Thrive.
- Attended a meeting, worked through till lunchtime.

### Kopan Monastery · twisty climb to silence
- Packed laptops, picked up the Thar, set out for **[Kopan Monastery](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Kopan+Monastery+Kathmandu)**.
- Approach starts on the **Kathmandu Ring Road**, then narrows into tiny winding streets. The final ascent is *single-vehicle-wide* with a gradient that felt like ~30°+ — properly thrilling drive.
- No on-premise parking. The guard pointed us to the road shoulder. Parked there, walked in.
- Inside: pure quiet. Walked the temples, gardens, stupas. Clicked sparingly — the place asks you to be still.

### Boudhanath route · lunch + the great stupa
- Drove down to the **Boudhanath sadak**. Stopped at **Coffee Himalayan & Himalaya Jewellery** for lunch + coffee + another office meeting.
- Then on to **[Boudhanath Stupa](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Boudhanath+Stupa+Kathmandu)** — my main worry was parking, but a **paid lot 400 m away** sorted it. Easy walk in.
- The stupa itself is a different scale of devotion — thousands of people circling, organised flow, full-hearted. Removed shoes, climbed the permitted inner levels, clicked a few pictures.

### Pashupatinath — and the Gate 3 scam to avoid
- Called my friend **Ayush** from outside Boudha — we worked together at the same Gurgaon company in 2018, my first job out of college, and I left in Dec 2018. He's Nepali, did B.Tech at MNIT Jaipur, now works at e-Sewa Kathmandu. *Hadn't seen him in ~8 years.* Asked him to meet us at Pashupatinath.
- Drove to **[Pashupatinath Temple · Gate 3](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Pashupatinath+Temple+Kathmandu)**. As we approached the gate, a young woman flagged us down and told us parking was 200 m further. Moved the car, parked. The *same woman* then showed up at the parking saying she runs a flower shop *"if we want"* to buy from. We followed her — *another man inside the shop, claiming Rajasthan origin*, explained Pashupatinath's offering customs (mainly rudraksha) and convinced us to pick up a small *tokri* of offerings. As we exited, the lady added that *we'd also need a different basket inside*, which we paid for too.
- **The lesson:** that whole sequence at **Gate 3 is a coordinated upsell scam**. Polite, friendly, well-rehearsed. They flag the parking, then route you into the shop, then layer the offerings. **Skip Gate 3 next time — go straight to Gate 1, which has free + large parking.** Don't buy anything from those shops. Nothing was needed inside.
- Inside the temple, called Ayush — he was at Gate 1. Coordinated, met up after eight years. Walked the full temple together with him as the unofficial guide. Sat inside for a while, caught up on the missing eight years.

### Dinner · Bajeko Sekuwa with Ayush
- Ayush picked the place: **[Bajeko Sekuwa · Sinamangal](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Bajeko+Sekuwa+Sinamangal+Kathmandu)** (the original outlet, near Tribhuvan airport). Mutton sekuwa with rice flakes — properly Nepali, *very* good.
- Drove there leaving his bike at the Gate 1 free parking. Late-lunch/early-dinner kind of meal.
- Dropped him back at Pashupatinath afterwards, said bye, headed back to Hotel Thrive.

### Thamel · second pass + the LOD experiment
- Parked at the hotel. Walked into Thamel on foot to give it another shot.
- Dinner #2 at **[Yala Cafe & Coffee Shop](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Yala+Cafe+Coffee+Shop+Thamel+Kathmandu)** — small, cute, lovely vibe. *Their momos are the reason to go* and they delivered.
- Decided to try Thamel's nightlife — walked into **[LOD · Lord of the Drinks](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=LOD+Lord+of+the+Drinks+Thamel+Kathmandu)** at 10:30 PM. Almost completely empty. Waiter said *crowd shows up later* — they did, slowly, but even by midnight it was thinly populated for a venue that big.
- Danced till 12:45 AM. DJ swapped sets, vibe dropped, took the cue and left. Tuk-tuk parked outside took us back to Hotel Thrive. Sleep.
entries.delta: Three of Kathmandu's headline sites done in an afternoon · plus an 8-year-late friend reunion at Pashupatinath.

events.text: Kopan Monastery · the road in is half the experience — narrows from ring road to single-vehicle alleys, last stretch is a ~30° climb. No on-site parking but the guard waves you to the road shoulder. Inside is total silence. Worth the drive.
Boudhanath Stupa · paid parking 400 m walk away solved the access problem. Removed shoes for the inner climb. Scale of devotion + organised flow = the closest thing to crowded-but-calm in Kathmandu.

Pashupatinath Gate 3 SCAM · a 'helpful' lady flags your car at the gate, redirects you 200 m to parking, then routes you to her flower shop where a man (claiming Rajasthan origin) sells offerings + a 'required' inner tokri. None of it is needed. SKIP GATE 3 entirely — use Gate 1 instead (free + large parking, no scam funnel).

Reunion at Pashupatinath · met Ayush after 8 years — we worked together in Gurgaon in 2018, my first job out of college. He's Nepali, MNIT Jaipur grad, now at e-Sewa in Kathmandu. Did the full temple tour together, sat and caught up. The kind of reconnection you don't plan and can't replace.

Bajeko Sekuwa · Sinamangal (the original outlet, near Tribhuvan airport). Mutton sekuwa with chiura (rice flakes) — properly Nepali, exactly the meal a local friend would pick. Worth the cross-town drive.
Yala Cafe & Coffee Shop · Thamel · the momos earn the reputation. Small, soft-lit, soothing vibe in a part of Thamel that's gentler than the main strip.

LOD · Lord of the Drinks (Thamel) — looked like Thamel's biggest nightlife venue on paper, half-empty in practice. Walked in at 10:30 PM near-deserted, crowd built slowly, still thin by midnight. DJ change at ~1 AM dropped the vibe. Not bad, just underwhelming for the size. Worth a stop if you're already passing, not worth a special trip.

entries.leg: Kathmandu · two Durbar Squares + deep work day
entries.route: Thamel → KTM Durbar Sq · work · Patan Durbar Sq · Garden of Dreams · OR2K
entries.notes:
Heavy office workload + tired legs from yesterday — designed today as **two short bursts of culture bracketing a long deep-work block**. Two of Nepal's three royal squares in the same day.

### Pre-breakfast · Kathmandu Durbar Square
- Up at **6 AM**, on the road to **[Kathmandu Durbar Square](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Kathmandu+Durbar+Square)** before the tour buses + tourist crowd showed up.
- Cloudy sky — no sun on the woodwork — but the atmosphere was *better* for being quieter. Wandered the courtyards mostly alone.
- The pieces that hit hardest:
  - The **Kaal Bhairav** statue — fierce, raw, you don't quite look away.
  - The **kneeling Hanuman** at the palace gate.
  - The old layered temple-architecture of the palace complex.
- Felt the *old culture and history of Kathmandu* in a way the modern Thamel chaos doesn't let through.

### Mid-day · the long work block
- Back to Hotel Thrive by **9:30 AM** for breakfast.
- Then **hard work and back-to-back office calls in the room till ~2:30 PM**.
- Lunch at **[Gokarna House Restaurant](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Gokarna+House+Restaurant+Thamel+Kathmandu)** (Paknajol, Thamel) — researched the **Thakali thali** reputation, ordered 1 veg + 1 mutton. Spices, aroma, presentation all on point. *Fell hard for Thakali food today.*
- Back to the hotel, more work through to **~7 PM**.

### Evening · Patan Durbar Square
- Crossed the Bagmati down to **[Patan Durbar Square](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Patan+Durbar+Square+Lalitpur)**.
- Two Durbar Squares in one day is its own kind of education. You start noticing the **layering** — Hindu + Buddhist iconography next to each other on the same wall, the same temple sometimes housing both traditions. The Newari architecture, the metal-work, the wood carving. Things that wouldn't exist this way side-by-side anywhere I've seen in India.
- Walked out properly curious about the **Hinduism / Buddhism relationship** — how the two co-evolved here in a way India's narrative usually keeps separate. Filing this for later reading.

### Detour · Garden of Dreams
- On the way back into Thamel, walked through **[Garden of Dreams](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Garden+of+Dreams+Kathmandu)** — the early-20th-century Neoclassical garden tucked behind Tridevi Marg.
- *Honest verdict: okayish but not worth a special visit.* Small footprint, neat pavilions, fine for a 20-minute breather if you're already passing — not a destination on its own. After the two Durbar squares the bar was high; this didn't clear it.

### Dinner · OR2K
- Walked into **[OR2K](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=OR2K+Thamel+Kathmandu)** in Thamel — vegetarian, Middle Eastern lean, cushion-floor seating (*shoes off at the door*). Highly rated, earned the rating. Hummus + falafel + Thali-Middle-Eastern hybrid plates.
- Back to Hotel Thrive. Sleep.
entries.delta: Two Durbar Squares + a full work day = the most productive day of the trip so far.

events.text: Kathmandu Durbar Square · go before 8 AM. Cloud cover beat sunshine for atmosphere — the courtyards are quieter, the carvings read better without the tour-bus crowd. Kaal Bhairav and the kneeling Hanuman are the must-sees.
Gokarna House (Paknajol, Thamel) · the Thakali thali set lives up to the research. Veg + mutton both excellent — proper Nepali plate, spice work that earns its reputation. New favourite cuisine.

Patan Durbar Square (Lalitpur) · the Newari architecture + the Hindu-Buddhist layering is the real lesson. Doing both Durbar Squares in one day makes the contrast (and the shared lineage) leap out — KTM = palace + worship, Patan = craft + co-existence.

Travel-induced curiosity logged · Hinduism / Buddhism co-evolution in Nepal is genuinely different from how India presents the two. The Newari temples carry both traditions visibly on the same structure. To research later — this is what travel is supposed to do.

Garden of Dreams · okayish, not worth a dedicated trip. Small site, neat Neoclassical pavilions, fine for a 20-min breather if you're already in central Thamel — but after both Durbar squares the contrast is unflattering. Skip unless it's already on your walking line.

OR2K · Thamel (Mandala Street) · vegetarian, Middle-Eastern lean, cushion-floor seating, shoes off at the door. Lives up to its 25-year rep. Easy dinner pick when you don't want another heavy meat plate.

entries.leg: Kathmandu · slow work day + Swayambhunath sunset
entries.notes:
Trip fatigue showing up — 11 days in, the kilometres + the altitude swing + the constant input were stacking up. Today was deliberately under-scheduled.

### Morning + afternoon · work block
- Breakfast at Hotel Thrive, back upstairs, **straight into office work from the room.** Originally thought we'd squeeze a museum visit in the morning — didn't happen, work won.
- Lunch break at **[Jasper Restaurant](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Jasper+Restaurant+Thamel+Kathmandu+Tridevi+Marga)** (Tridevi Marga, Thamel) — multi-cuisine, cosy. Good reviews delivered.
- Back at the laptop till **~5:30 PM**. Most museums were already closed by the time we were free; museums went on the *skipped this time* pile.

### Sunset · Swayambhunath
- Took the Thar to **[Swayambhunath](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Swayambhunath+Monkey+Temple+Kathmandu)** — the eye-stupa on its own hill west of the city. A *chilled* trip on purpose, no checklist energy.
- Climbed the long stair set up the hill. Slow pace, no pressure.
- Up top: the painted eyes, the **Shantipur peace statue**, monks moving through, the Boudha-meets-Hindu mix of shrines and prayer wheels, **monkeys everywhere** living up to the temple's other name.
- Sat for a while just looking at Kathmandu spread out below. Took me back to **January when this whole "drive to Nepal" idea first showed up in my head** — and here we were, half a year later, on a hill above the city, having come overland from Bikaner via Muktinath. Quietly unreal moment.

### Dinner · Forest & Plate
- Drove back, parked the Thar at the hotel, walked into Thamel on foot.
- Early dinner at **[Forest & Plate](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Forest+and+Plate+Mandala+Street+Thamel)** (3rd floor, Sagarmatha Complex, Mandala Street) — rooftop, fresh + organic lean, stupa-view garden vibe.
- Back to the hotel. **In bed by 10:30** — early by trip standards, exactly right.
entries.delta: Pulled the throttle back on purpose · trip fatigue real, recovery day banked before the Chitwan run.

events.text: Work-day discipline · skipped the morning museum plan because work asked for the hours. The right call — trip fatigue was real and forcing a tourist agenda would've burned the evening Swayambhunath energy too.
Jasper Restaurant (Tridevi Marga, Thamel) · cosy multi-cuisine lunch spot, lives up to its review reputation. Their goat shank gets specific praise online; we kept it lighter for the workday.

Swayambhunath at sunset · the eye-stupa earns the hype. The stair climb is the warm-up; the view of Kathmandu from the top is the payoff. Plenty of monkeys (live up to the 'Monkey Temple' name), the Shantipur peace statue, prayer wheels, the Hindu-Buddhist mix in one campus.

Trip-arc moment · sitting on the Swayambhunath hill thinking back to January when 'drive to Nepal' first surfaced as an idea. Bikaner → Muktinath → Kathmandu, overland, in our own car. The map closed on itself.

Forest & Plate (Sagarmatha Complex, Mandala St, Thamel — 3rd floor rooftop) · organic-lean menu, garden vibe, view over the lit-up Thamel rooftops. Lighter-than-Thakali dinner choice when you've had enough heavy plates.
